renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: broad_peak_significance
  title: Broad region significance along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a broad region at its centre: the chromosome and position on the horizontal axis and its mean significance, as minus log10 of the q-value, on the vertical axis, coloured by sample. It answers where the broad domains lie and how confident each call is.
    How to read: tall points are the most confident regions, and a column of points across samples is a domain called in several libraries. For a broad call the q-value is the mean over the whole region and not a value at a summit. Open the table to inspect a labelled region.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is a q-value of 0.05, the default q-value cut-off of MACS2 callpeak, shown as 1.301 on this axis. MACS2 also links nearby regions with a separate broad cut-off, and its documentation suggests 0.01 as the q-value for broad marks, so a run may use a stricter line.
    Source: https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html
  kind: manhattan
  config:
    score_kind: -log10 q-value
    score_threshold: 1.30103
    color_by_columns:
    - sample
    default_color_by: sample
    hover_cols:
    - fold_enrichment
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    chr: chr
    pos: midpoint
    score: neg_log10_qvalue
    feature: peak_id

- component: figure
  title: Region width per sample
  description: |-
    Each box is a sample: the spread of the widths of its broad regions, on a logarithmic axis, coloured by sample. It answers how wide the called domains are and whether samples differ.
    How to read: broad calls are meant for histone marks, whose domains are wider than transcription factor peaks. Compare replicates with each other, since a sample with much narrower regions than its replicates was probably called differently.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median region width of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of MACS2.
    Source: https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: width
    color: sample
    log_y: 'True'
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      width: Region width (bp)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: width

- component: card
  title: Broad regions called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of broad regions in view, with the number of samples that called them, and the bars rank the chromosomes holding most. It answers how many domains are called and where they concentrate.
    How to read: large chromosomes hold more regions simply by length. A chromosome far above that expectation is worth a look.
  column: sample
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: chr
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: regions, by chromosome

- component: card
  title: Region width
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median region width in base pairs, with the lower and upper quartiles. It answers how broad the domains are.
    How to read: widths span orders of magnitude, so the quartiles tell more than a single number. Compare samples of the same mark with each other.
  column: width
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - q1
  - q3
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median width, with its quartiles

- component: card
  title: Fold enrichment
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean fold enrichment of the regions, with its median and maximum, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how strong the enrichment is overall.
    How to read: for a broad call the enrichment is a mean over the region, so it is lower than for a narrow peak. A mean close to the median means few extreme regions.
    Source: https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html
  column: fold_enrichment
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: fold enrichment, distribution

- component: card
  title: Weakest region significance
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest minus log10 q-value of any region in view, compared with the cut-off, with the median and the highest alongside. It answers whether every region clears the standard cut-off.
    How to read: a minimum above the line means all regions pass, which is expected when the caller used its default. A minimum below it means the run called regions at a looser cut-off.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off is a q-value of 0.05, the default of MACS2 callpeak, shown as 1.301 on the minus log10 scale.
    Source: https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html
  column: neg_log10_qvalue
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 1.30103
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: weakest region against the q-value cut-off

- component: table
  title: Broad region table
  description: |-
    Each row is a broad region with its sample, position, width, centre, fold enrichment and the minus log10 p-value and q-value MACS2 reported. It answers which regions to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by significance or by width, and filter by sample or chromosome.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: peak_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: consensus_upset
  title: Consensus peaks shared between samples
  description: |-
    Each bar is a combination of samples and its height is the number of consensus intervals called in exactly those samples. It answers how reproducible the peak set is between replicates and conditions.
    How to read: tall bars over all replicates of one condition are reproducible peaks. Tall bars over a single sample are private peaks that no other sample supports. Bars over samples of different conditions are shared binding sites.
    Lines and annotations: bars are coloured by the number of samples in the combination, so private and widely shared intervals separate at a glance.
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree

- component: card
  title: Consensus intervals
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of consensus sets in view with the intervals they hold, and the bars rank the sets by how many intervals they contain. It answers how large each consensus peak set is.
    How to read: a set with few intervals has little reproducible signal. Compare sets of the same assay.
  column: consensus_set
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: consensus_set
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: intervals, by consensus set

- component: card
  title: Samples per interval
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean number of samples that call a peak on an interval, and the box shows its spread. It answers how reproducible the intervals are.
    How to read: a mean near one means most intervals are called in one sample only. A mean near the number of replicates means a reproducible peak set.
  column: num_samples
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: samples per interval, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Peaks merged into intervals
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of peak calls merged into the consensus intervals, with the mean and the largest per interval, and the histogram shows how many peaks each interval merges. It answers how much the merging collapses.
    How to read: an interval that merges many peaks is either a wide enriched region or several nearby peaks joined, so open the interval before treating it as one site.
  column: num_peaks
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - average
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: peaks merged per interval, distribution

- component: card
  title: Intervals by consensus set
  description: |-
    Each unit is one consensus interval, with the number of sets as the secondary number, and the ring splits the intervals by set. It answers how the intervals divide between the sets.
    How to read: a set that takes most of the ring contributes most of the peaks to the consensus.
  column: consensus_set
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: consensus_set
  caption: intervals, by consensus set

- component: table
  title: Consensus interval table
  description: |-
    Each row is a consensus interval with its set, position, the number of peaks merged into it, the number of samples that call it and a 0/1 flag per sample. It answers which intervals are shared and by whom, and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by the number of samples to list the most reproducible intervals.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: peak_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: consensus_signal_heatmap
  title: Fold enrichment of consensus peaks
  description: |-
    Each cell is a consensus interval in a sample: the MACS2 fold enrichment of the peak called there, or 0 where the sample called none. Rows and columns are clustered. It answers which intervals are bound in which samples and how strongly.
    How to read: columns that cluster together are samples with a similar binding profile, such as replicates or one condition. Blocks of colour in one group of samples only are condition-specific sites. A sample with pale rows against its replicates has weaker enrichment.
    Lines and annotations: the strips beside the rows name the consensus set and the number of samples that call the interval. Only the intervals with the largest summed enrichment per set are drawn.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: region
    row_annotation_cols:
    - consensus_set
    - support

- component: card
  title: Strongest consensus intervals
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of consensus sets in view with the strongest intervals they contribute, and the bars rank the sets. It answers which sets supply the most strongly bound intervals.
    How to read: a set that dominates the ranking has the strongest enrichment. Only the top intervals per set are kept, so the counts are not the full peak sets.
  column: consensus_set
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: consensus_set
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: strongest intervals, by consensus set

- component: card
  title: Support per interval
  description: |-
    Each unit is a strongly bound interval, with the number of distinct support levels as the secondary number, and the ring splits the intervals by how many samples call them. It answers how widely the strongest intervals are supported.
    How to read: a ring dominated by the highest support means the strongest peaks are reproducible across samples. A large share with support of one means strong peaks private to a sample.
  column: support
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: support
  caption: intervals, by number of supporting samples

- component: table
  title: Consensus enrichment table
  description: |-
    Each row is a consensus interval with its set, region, the number of supporting samples and its fold enrichment in every sample. It answers the exact values behind the heatmap.
    How to read: sort by a sample column to list the intervals it binds most strongly.

- component: figure
  title: Fraction of reads in peaks per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample: the fraction of its mapped reads that fall inside the called peaks. It answers how much of the signal in each library is enrichment and not background.
    How to read: a higher bar means a better signal to noise, and replicates should be close. A bar far below its replicates marks a weak library. ENCODE says that FRiP has no defined threshold and is useful for comparing similar experiments, so compare samples of the same assay and antibody.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median fraction of reads in peaks of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of MACS2.
    Source: https://www.encodeproject.org/data-standards/chip-seq/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: frip_score
    color: sample
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      frip_score: Fraction of reads in peaks
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: frip_score

- component: card
  title: Peaks called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of peaks over the samples in view, and the box shows the quartiles of peaks per sample. It answers how many regions the libraries yield.
    How to read: replicates should give similar counts. A sample far below its replicates has weak or shallow signal. Peak counts depend on depth, so read them beside the FRiP bars.
  column: num_peaks
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: peaks per sample, with their spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Mean FRiP
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean fraction of reads in peaks over the samples in view, and the box shows its spread. It answers how enriched the libraries are on average.
    How to read: a wide box means the libraries differ in enrichment. ENCODE defines no cut-off for it, so judge a sample against its replicates and its assay.
    Source: https://www.encodeproject.org/data-standards/terms/
  column: frip_score
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: FRiP, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Median peak width
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of each sample's median peak width, and the box shows its spread. It answers how broad the called peaks are.
    How to read: replicates should have similar widths, and the expected width depends on the mark. A sample that differs from its replicates may be called with different settings.
  column: width_median
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median peak width, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Median fold enrichment
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of each sample's median peak fold enrichment, and the box shows its spread. It answers how strong the typical peak is against its control.
    How to read: MACS2 publishes no minimum for fold enrichment, so compare samples with their replicates. A low value with a high peak count suggests many weak peaks.
  column: fold_enrichment_median
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median fold enrichment, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Peak QC table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its peak count, FRiP score and the median, mean and maximum of peak width, fold enrichment and significance. It answers the exact quality numbers behind the bars and cards.
    How to read: sort by FRiP or by peak count to find the weak libraries.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: peak_significance
  title: Peak significance along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a peak at its summit position: the chromosome and position on the horizontal axis and its significance, as minus log10 of the q-value, on the vertical axis, coloured by sample. It answers where the strongest calls lie and whether samples call the same regions.
    How to read: tall points are the most confident peaks, and a column of points across samples is a region called in several libraries. Peak calls from one sample sit in a dense band just above the cut-off, so read this tile for positions and not for the density of calls. Open the table to inspect a labelled peak.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is a q-value of 0.05, the default q-value cut-off of MACS2 callpeak, shown as 1.301 on this axis. A run can set its own cut-off, and the line then no longer matches what the caller used.
    Source: https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html
  kind: manhattan
  config:
    score_kind: -log10 q-value
    score_threshold: 1.30103
    color_by_columns:
    - sample
    default_color_by: sample
    hover_cols:
    - fold_enrichment
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    chr: chr
    pos: summit
    score: neg_log10_qvalue
    feature: peak_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: peak_genome_view
  title: Peaks on the genome
  description: |-
    Each rectangle is a peak drawn over its interval on a chromosome-aware axis, with its height set by significance and its colour by sample. It answers where peaks cluster along the chromosomes and which libraries share them.
    How to read: zoom into a region to compare libraries. Peaks stacked on the same interval in several samples are reproducible, and an interval called in one sample only is private to it. Peaks are intervals, so wide ones show as long blocks.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal rule is a q-value of 0.05, the default q-value cut-off of MACS2 callpeak, shown as 1.301 on this axis.
    Source: https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    score_title: -log10 q-value
    score_threshold: 1.30103
  roles:
    chr: chr
    pos: start
    score: neg_log10_qvalue
    feature: peak_id
    end: end
    sample: sample
    category: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: peak_coverage_track
  title: Peak enrichment along the genome
  description: |-
    Each mark is a peak placed on its chromosome, with its fold enrichment at the summit over the local background on the vertical axis, one colour per sample. It answers how strong the enrichment is along the genome and where libraries agree.
    How to read: higher marks are peaks with more signal over the control, and overlapping marks of different colours are peaks found in several samples. Pick a chromosome to read it in detail.
    Note: MACS2 reports the fold enrichment at the peak summit against a Poisson background with the local lambda, so values are comparable only within a run.
    Source: https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html
  kind: coverage_track
  config:
    color_by: sample
    smoothing_window: 0
  roles:
    chromosome: chr
    position: start
    value: fold_enrichment
    end: end
    sample: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: peak_volcano
  title: Enrichment against significance
  description: |-
    Each point is a peak: its fold enrichment at the summit on the horizontal axis and its significance, as minus log10 of the q-value, on the vertical axis, coloured by sample. It answers which peaks are both strongly enriched and confidently called.
    How to read: peaks in the upper right are strong and confident, and are the ones to follow up. A peak with high enrichment but low significance sits in a region with few reads, and the reverse is a broad, modest enrichment. Open the table for the labelled peaks.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is a q-value of 0.05, the default q-value cut-off of MACS2 callpeak. The vertical line is a fold enrichment of 1, which means no enrichment over the local background by definition of the ratio.
    Source: https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_is_neg_log10: true
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_threshold: 1.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Fold enrichment
    significance_label: -log10 q-value
  roles:
    feature_id: peak_id
    effect_size: fold_enrichment
    significance: neg_log10_qvalue
    label: peak_id
    category: sample

- component: figure
  title: Peak width per sample
  description: |-
    Each box is a sample: the spread of the widths of its peaks, on a logarithmic axis, coloured by sample. It answers how wide the called regions are and whether samples differ.
    How to read: MACS2 calls narrow peaks for transcription factor ChIP-seq and broad regions for histone marks, so the expected width depends on the mark. A sample with a very different width than its replicates may have been called with different settings or has a different signal to noise.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median peak width of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of MACS2.
    Source: https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: width
    color: sample
    log_y: 'True'
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      width: Peak width (bp)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: width

- component: card
  title: Peaks called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of peaks in view, with the number of samples that called them, and the bars rank the chromosomes holding most. It answers how many regions are called and where they concentrate.
    How to read: large chromosomes hold more peaks simply by length. A chromosome that stands out far above that expectation is worth a look.
  column: sample
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: chr
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: peaks, by chromosome

- component: card
  title: Peak width
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median peak width in base pairs, with the lower and upper quartiles. It answers how narrow or broad the calls are.
    How to read: the expected width depends on the mark, so compare samples of the same assay. Widths span orders of magnitude, so the quartiles tell more than a box.
    Source: https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html
  column: width
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - q1
  - q3
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median width, with its quartiles

- component: card
  title: Fold enrichment
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean fold enrichment of peak summits, with its median and maximum, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how strong the enrichment is overall.
    How to read: a distribution piled near the lower end with a long right tail is typical. A mean close to the median means few extreme peaks.
  column: fold_enrichment
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: fold enrichment, distribution

- component: card
  title: Weakest peak significance
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest minus log10 q-value of any peak in view, compared with the cut-off, with the median and the highest alongside. It answers whether every peak clears the standard cut-off.
    How to read: a minimum above the line means all peaks pass, which is expected when the caller used its default. A minimum below it means the run called peaks at a looser cut-off.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off is a q-value of 0.05, the default of MACS2 callpeak, shown as 1.301 on the minus log10 scale.
    Source: https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html
  column: neg_log10_qvalue
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 1.30103
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: weakest peak against the q-value cut-off

- component: table
  title: Peak table
  description: |-
    Each row is a peak with its sample, position, width, summit, fold enrichment and the minus log10 p-value and q-value MACS2 reported. It answers which peaks to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by significance or by fold enrichment, and filter by sample or chromosome.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: peak_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: summit_concordance_profile
  title: Summit agreement between samples
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sample: how densely the summits called in the other samples fall around its own summits, by distance from the summit. It answers whether independent libraries place their peaks on the same sites.
    How to read: a sharp spike at the centre means the other samples put their summits on this sample's summits, so replicates agree or factors share sites. A flat curve means they do not. The count is over every other sample of the run, so filter to a comparison of interest.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical marker at zero is the summit of each anchor peak, which is the centre of the window by construction. This is an aggregate of peak calls and not a read coverage signal.
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Distance from summit (bp)
    y_title: Other samples' summits per kb
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: Summit
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: offset_bp
    y: neighbour_summit_density

- component: advanced_viz
  id: summit_footprint_profile
  title: Average peak footprint
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sample: the share of its peaks whose called interval covers each position, by distance from their own summit. It answers how wide the typical peak is around its summit.
    How to read: the curve is one at the summit and falls as peaks end. A curve that drops within a few hundred base pairs is a sharp, transcription factor like sample, and one that stays high for kilobases is a broad mark. The distance at which a curve crosses one half is the median half-width of its peaks.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical marker at zero is the summit of each peak, the centre of the window by construction.
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Distance from summit (bp)
    y_title: Share of peaks covering the position
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: Summit
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: offset_bp
    y: peak_footprint

- component: figure
  title: Other samples' summits around each summit
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: how densely the summits of the other samples fall around its own summits, by distance from the summit. It answers the same question as the profile above in a plain line chart.
    How to read: a central peak means agreement between libraries, and a flat line at the background means none. Compare the lines of replicates, which should overlap.
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: offset_bp
    y: neighbour_summit_density
    color: sample
    labels:
      offset_bp: Distance from summit (bp)
      neighbour_summit_density: Other samples' summits per kb
      sample: Sample

- component: card
  title: Peak summit agreement
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest density of other samples' summits found around an anchor summit, with the median and the lowest across bins. It answers how strongly libraries concentrate their summits on the same sites.
    How to read: a maximum far above the median means a central spike, so summits agree. A maximum close to the median is a flat curve with no agreement.
  column: neighbour_summit_density
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: highest density, with the median and lowest

- component: card
  title: Peak footprint
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of peaks covering a position in the window, and the box shows its spread. It answers how far the typical peak extends from its summit.
    How to read: a high median means peaks cover most of the window, which is typical of broad calls. A low median means narrow peaks.
  column: peak_footprint
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: footprint share, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Summit profile table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample at one distance from the summit, with the number of anchor summits, the peak footprint and the density of other samples' summits. It answers the exact values behind the curves.
    How to read: filter to one sample and sort by distance to read its profile.
